Add a D3 acceptance case for a worktree with a root AGENTS.md and no CLAUDE.md. Delete Open risks line 3 (Claude Code's support for CLAUDE.local.md is assumed...), since the fact is now recorded in D3.

Extend D9's first bullet's import argument to cover the runproc edge, and keep the D9 acceptance criterion that runproc.HubOwner derives from the one declaration.

In D6, state where a seam failure in a detached process lands and what bounds it: for example the detached sync writes a friction note or a creel notice to the hub naming the worktree and lym heddle render as the way forward, or D6 states plainly that a detached failure is log-only and that the stale file stays until the next take-in of a re-render path or a hand render. Add the matching D6 acceptance case.

In D4, make the closure return the place, the three cheap values, the machine's buttons and a separate function that resolves {beam}, which the render calls only when an entry of the composed row uses {beam}.

In D1, either let a block row's on_done be empty, rewritten like any inlined row's to the enclosing block's exit (and refused empty outside every block), or add a Bound line saying a sub-recipe cannot end in a block. Add a nested-block row to the D2 acceptance bullet: a parent holding a block whose recipe holds a block expands with each inner row's path outer/inner and each empty on_done set to its innermost block's exit.

The parent obtains the operator's approval of the name arras, or a replacement name, and records it with lym loom decision add; the writer then drops the Open risks line and marks Q8 resolved.

Extend the plan-writer note on internal/shedengine/entry.go to name the goto admission in internal/shedengine/goto.go as a second reader.
Add to D2's refusal list: a block row whose on_done names the block row itself or a row its own expansion inlines. Add that case to the D2 refusals acceptance bullet.

Change the sentence 'Each refusal names the part to fix and that its writer fixes it' so it names the part to fix and says the chair has its writer fix it, or fixes it itself when that writer no longer answers (D9). Add to D11 that a part writer never runs lym loom join-parts or lym loom insert-card. Extend the D8 acceptance criterion with refusals for a blocked run at the row and for a caller that is not the chair.

In D6, replace the sentence beginning 'A writer that failed to start or died stays an error' with a mapping for every way a writer seat ends the step: a writer that timed out maps to Stuck with its first output path as pointer and a reason naming the seat, its part and the timeout; a writer that failed to start maps to an error wrapping shuttleengine.ErrNotStarted carrying the writer's StartError; a writer that died maps to an error wrapping shuttleengine.ErrAgentDied naming the writer seat, not the chair. State that MultiLLMProducer reads the ended seat's SeatResult (EndedStep, Outcome, StartError) before the chair's result, so the stopped chair's outcome never decides these cases.
